source_lines_after.36: Assume AC. For every $d,e\ge0$, let $X_d=(\mathbb{RP}^L)^{d+1}$, $X_e=(\mathbb{RP}^L)^{e+1}$, with $L\ge\max(d,e)+1$ and $P_d=\prod x_i$, $P_e=\prod y_j$. The map $A^d\otimes A^e\to H^*(X_d;\mathbb F_2)\otimes H^*(X_e;\mathbb F_2)$, $a\otimes b\mapsto a(P_d)\otimes b(P_e)$, is injective; under Künneth, external products jointly detect every homogeneous tensor of square operations.
source_lines_after.52: 1.1 Let $A^d$ be the degree-$d$ part of the square algebra. By the admissible-basis theorem, its basis consists of $\mathrm{Sq}^I$ with $|I|=d$. Set $X_d=(\mathbb{RP}^L)^{d+1}$, $P_d=x_1\cdots x_{d+1}$, with $L\ge d+1$. Every admissible $I$ of degree $d$ has $e(I)\le d<d+1$. The leading-monomial lemma therefore applies and gives distinct largest monomials for the classes $\mathrm{Sq}^I(P_d)$. Those classes are linearly independent: in a nonzero finite linear combination, the largest of the distinct leading monomials cannot cancel. Thus evaluation $j_d:A^d\to H^*(X_d;\mathbb F_2)$, $a\mapsto a(P_d)$, is injective. For $d=0$, $X_0=\mathbb{RP}^L$ and $P_0=x_1$; the identity operation sends $x_1$ to the nonzero class $x_1$. [given, F1]
source_lines_after.54: 2.1 The map $j_d\otimes j_e$ is injective for an explicit linear-algebra reason. Extend bases of $\operatorname{im}(j_d)$ and $\operatorname{im}(j_e)$ to bases of the two target vector spaces. Projection to $\operatorname{im}(j_d)$, followed by $j_d^{-1}$, gives a left inverse $r_d$ of $j_d$; similarly obtain $r_e$. Then $r_d\otimes r_e$ is a left inverse of $j_d\otimes j_e$ by the tensor universal property, so $j_d\otimes j_e$ is injective. The cohomological Künneth theorem identifies the target with the corresponding external-product subspace in $H^*(X_d\times X_e;\mathbb F_2)$. Distinct bidegrees remain distinct under this Künneth decomposition. Since every tensor is a finite sum of homogeneous bidegrees, an element of $A\otimes A$ acting as zero on every external product of classes must be zero. This proves tensor faithfulness. [step 1.1, F2, F3] ∎
